root.label: Lock-free programming
root.note: Replace locks with CAS retry loops; pay for it with ABA and memory reclamation.

children.label: Progress guarantees
children.note: Blocking, obstruction-free, lock-free and wait-free, from weakest to strongest.

children.label: Lock-free
children.note: Some thread always finishes; an individual thread may starve.

children.label: Wait-free
children.note: Every thread finishes in a bounded number of its own steps.

children.label: What the standard requires
children.note: [intro.progress] requires obstruction-freedom and only encourages lock-freedom.

children.label: atomic_flag
children.note: The only type guaranteed lock-free; ask is_always_lock_free for others.

children.label: Treiber stack
children.note: A linked list with an atomic head, updated by CAS loops.

children.label: Push
children.note: Link the private node to the head, CAS the head to it; a failed CAS refreshes next.

children.label: Pop
children.note: CAS the head to head->next; reading next of a freed node is UB.

children.label: compare_exchange_weak
children.note: Right inside a retry loop, since spurious failure costs one iteration.

children.label: ABA problem
children.note: A CAS succeeds because the pointer value came back, though the structure changed.

children.label: Recycled node
children.note: Pop A, pop B, push A again: a stale CAS installs the removed B.

children.label: Tagged pointers
children.note: A counter beside the pointer, updated by double-width CAS, defeats ABA.

children.label: Not reclamation
children.note: Tags stop the wrong CAS but not a dereference of freed memory.

children.label: Safe reclamation
children.note: Delay freeing a node until no thread can still hold a pointer to it.

children.label: Hazard pointers
children.note: Publish the pointer before use; retired nodes are freed when no slot holds them.

children.label: RCU and epochs
children.note: Cheap readers; writers wait for a grace period before freeing.

children.label: atomic<shared_ptr>
children.note: C++20; reference counts prevent reuse, but libstdc++'s is not lock-free.

children.label: C++26 support
children.note: <hazard_pointer> and <rcu> standardize the first two schemes.

children.label: Memory orders in CAS
children.note: Choose success and failure orders by what the thread does with the value.

children.label: Push orders
children.note: Success release to publish the node; failure relaxed.

children.label: Pop orders
children.note: Acquire on success and failure, because the reloaded pointer is dereferenced.

children.label: Failure restrictions
children.note: Never release or acq_rel; since C++17 it may be stronger than success.

children.label: Performance
children.note: Lock-free is a progress property, not a speed guarantee.

children.label: Contention
children.note: Every failed CAS still takes the cache line; a mutex can win.

children.label: False sharing
children.note: Independent atomics on one cache line slow each other but never race.

children.label: Linearizability
children.note: Each operation appears atomic at one point; for Treiber, the successful CAS.
